name: MRN platform
full_name: MRI-based magnetic resonance navigation platform steering bead-tipped catheters and guidewires with added gradient coils
group: Martel, NanoRobotics Laboratory, Polytechnique Montreal (with Soulez, CHUM, for the animal study)
versions: 2011: catheter with ferromagnetic spheres steered by MRI gradients, deflection characterised (gosselin2011_characterization, review-only); MRN platform with a propulsion and imaging coil insert in a 1.5-T Siemens Sonata (vonthron2011_mri); 2015: guidewire with a ferromagnetic bead steered in 2 rabbits (lalande2015_vivo, abstract)
target_anatomy: selective catheterization of aortic branches (renal, superior mesenteric and iliac arteries) in rabbits (lalande2015_vivo abstract)
devices_driven: 2.5 Fr catheter (FasTracker 018, Boston Scientific) with two 0.9 mm chrome-steel beads 1.6 mm apart (vonthron2011_mri Sec. VII-A); guidewire with a magnetic bead at its tip (lalande2015_vivo abstract)
n_dof_detail: 3D gradient force on the tip bead (three propulsion gradient axes, vonthron2011_mri Sec. IV)
translation_detail: magnetic (gradient-force steering of the tip); advance N.R. in the abstract (manual per li2020_magnetic Sec. 4.1: 'blindly controlled' between tracking sequences)
rotation_detail: gradient direction of the added coils
footprint_mm: N.R. (coil insert inside a clinical 1.5-T bore, vonthron2011_mri Fig. 2)
imaging_compat: MRI tracking sequence interleaved with propulsion (imaging and propulsion mutually exclusive, vonthron2011_mri Fig. 3); MRA roadmap and dedicated tracking (lalande2015_vivo abstract)
validation_detail: 2 rabbits: selective catheterization of right and left renal arteries successful and reproducible, SMA and iliac feasible, no inadvertent side-branch entry when advanced without actuation (lalande2015_vivo abstract); catheter deflection in a water bath for gradients -400 to +400 mT/m in Maxwell coils and in the propulsion insert (vonthron2011_mri Sec. VII-A, Figs. 5-7)
key_numbers: propulsion insert up to 450 mT/m in three directions; minimum coil rise time 20 ms; clinical imaging gradients about 20 mT/m effective (40 mT/m nominal) on a Siemens Sonata (vonthron2011_mri Sec. III-IV)
